Returns the user templates in review, public, rejected or blocked, if the requesting user is staff: the revision under review of a template in review or rejected, the public revision of a public one, otherwise its latest revision. The templates can be searched by name and by the name or email of the author.
Returns how many user templates are in review, public, rejected and blocked, if the requesting user is staff.

Approves a user template in review or rejected, if the requesting user is staff: the revision they reviewed is listed for everybody on this instance in place of the one listed until then. It must still be the revision under review, not reviewed since, have content, and not be edited since it was submitted, and the state they saw, and whether it was listed, must still be the template's.

Blocks a user template in any state, if the requesting user is staff. Only its author and instance admins can open it, only instance admins can install or download it, its private link stops working, and its author sees the reason and can't change its visibility or private link. Nothing else changes. Blocking a blocked template changes the reason.

Rejects a user template in review, or a listed one, if the requesting user is staff. A listed template is taken out of the listing, unless only its edit is in review: then only the edit is rejected. The revision they reviewed must still be the template's row, not reviewed since, and the state they saw, and whether it was listed, must still be the template's. Its author sees the reason, and its next submit goes to review.

Lifts the block of a user template, if the requesting user is staff. The template is private afterwards, with its private link working again, and its author can make it public again. Unblocking a template that isn't blocked changes nothing.
Returns all users with detailed information on each user, if the requesting user is staff.
Creates and returns a new user if the requesting user is staff. This works even if new signups are disabled.

This endpoint allows staff to impersonate another user by requesting a JWT token and user object. The requesting user must have staff access in order to do this. It's not possible to impersonate a superuser, staff or deactivated user.
Deletes the specified user, if the requesting user has admin permissions. You cannot delete yourself.
Updates specified user attributes and returns the updated user if the requesting user is staff. You cannot update yourself to no longer be an admin or active.

Removes the configured two-factor authentication of the specified user, if the requesting user is staff. This can be used to restore access for users that lost their two-factor device and backup codes. The user will be able to log in with just their password and can configure two-factor authentication again afterwards.

Moves the trigger to the trash, where it can be restored. Requires permission to update the agent and read its configuration.

Updates the provided fields of the trigger: its name, its switch, its message, its overlap rule and the values of its service, whose type is fixed. Switching it off cancels its queued replies. Requires permission to update the agent and read its configuration.

Lists all the rows of the table related to the provided parameter if the user has access to the related database's workspace. The response is paginated by a page/size style. It is also possible to provide an optional search query, only rows where the data matches the search query are going to be returned then. The properties of the returned rows depends on which fields the table has. For a complete overview of fields use the **list_database_table_fields** endpoint to list them all. In the example all field types are listed, but normally the number in field_{id} key is going to be the id of the field. Or if the GET parameter `user_field_names` is provided then the keys will be the name of the field. The value is what the user has provided and the format of it depends on the fields type.

If you want to add a value for the field with for example id `10`, the key must be named `field_10`. Or instead if the `user_field_names` GET param is provided the key must be the name of the field. Of course multiple fields can be provided in one request. In the examples below you will find all the different field types, the numbers/ids in the example are just there for example purposes, the field_ID must be replaced with the actual id of the field or the name of the field if `user_field_names` is provided.

The `view` query parameter selects the shape of the response:

- `view=flat`: a paginated list of the official templates and the user templates the caller can open, most recently changed first, filtered with `type`, `owned`, `listed`, `category` and `search`. A user template shows the latest revision the caller can open, or its public revision with `listed=true`. `state`, `reason`, `source_workspace_id`, `source_application_ids` and `install_count` are only set for the owner of a user template.
- `view=public_categories`: the categories holding at least one public user template, ignoring the other query parameters. Official templates aren't taken into account.

Start an async job to install the applications of the given template into the given workspace if the user has access to that workspace. The response contains those newly created applications.

A user template can be installed by its owner, by the instance admins, by anyone signed in while it's public, and by anyone signed in with the token of its private link. Only the instance admins can install a blocked one. While it's public, everyone installs its public revision, and its owner the latest revision with `latest`. While it isn't public, everyone who can install it installs the latest revision. The `template_id` is the id of the template, not of one of its revisions.

Deletes a user template. Its owner can delete it in any state, and an instance admin can delete any user template. It's gone for everybody right away, and its revisions and content are removed later. The applications installed from it are kept. This can't be undone.

Updates a user template owned by the user. With `visibility` `public`, its latest revision goes to review, and once an instance admin approves it, it's listed, with the name of its author, for everybody on this instance, who can open it. Signed-in users can install it. It's listed right away only when approval isn't required and no admin rejected the template since it was last approved. The author must agree to that with `public_listing_consent`. The `state` of the response tells whether it's listed or in review. With `visibility` `private`, it isn't listed anymore, its revision in review or rejected is withdrawn, and only its owner and anyone with its private link can open and install it. Nothing changes when a template whose latest revision is listed or in review is made public, or when a template that isn't listed and has nothing in review or rejected is made private. With `private_link`, instead of `visibility`, the private link of the template is created or turned off, and its token is in `private_link_token`. Anyone with the link can preview the template, also signed out, and install or download it once signed in. Turning the link off stops it from working, and a public template stays public. Asking for the link it has changes nothing. The visibility and the private link of a blocked template can't be changed.

A user template can be downloaded by whoever can install it. Its owner and the instance admins may download any revision of it. Anyone else downloads the public revision, or the latest one of a template that isn't public with the token of its private link in the `Baserow-Template-Authorization` header: when another revision than the one shown is that one since, `ERROR_TEMPLATE_UPDATED` is responded with.

Replaces the token of the private link of a user template owned by the user, which takes the access away from everybody who has the old link. The new token is in `private_link_token`. A template without a private link keeps having none. The private link of a blocked template can't be changed.

Changes one or more preferences of the authenticated user, such as the default sort order of a listing page. Preferences that are not provided keep their value. Responds with all preferences.

Redoes the latest redoable action performed by the user making the request. a ClientSessionId header must be provided and only actions which were performed the same user with the same ClientSessionId value set on the api request that performed the action will be redone.Additionally the ClientSessionId header must be between 1 and 256 characters long and must only contain alphanumeric or the - characters.

Changes the password of a user if the reset token is valid. The **send_password_reset_email** endpoint sends an email to the user containing the token. That token can be used to change the password here without providing the old password.
Schedules the account deletion of the authenticated user. The user will be permanently deleted after the grace delay defined by the instance administrator.
Sends an email to the new email address containing a confirmation link. The user must provide their current password to initiate this request. The link is going to be valid for 12 hours.

Sends an email containing the password reset link to the email address of the user. This will only be done if a user is found with the given email address. The endpoint will not fail if the email address is not found. The link is going to the valid for 2 hours.
Sends an email to the user with an email verification link if the user's email is not verified yet.

Authenticates an existing user based on their email and their password. If successful, an access token and a refresh token will be returned. If the account is protected with two-factor authentication, temporary token is returned to finish the verification.
Blacklists the provided token. This can be used the sign the user off.

Generate a new access_token that can be used to continue operating on Baserow starting from a valid refresh token. Unless refresh token rotation is disabled, the response also contains a new refresh_token that must be used for the next refresh. The provided refresh token stops working after 30 seconds, and using it after that signs the session off.
Verifies if the refresh token is valid and can be used to generate a new access_token.

undoes the latest undoable action performed by the user making the request. a ClientSessionId header must be provided and only actions which were performed the same user with the same ClientSessionId value set on the api request that performed the action will be undone.Additionally the ClientSessionId header must be between 1 and 256 characters long and must only contain alphanumeric or the - characters.

Passing the correct verification token will confirm that the user's email address belongs to the user. This endpoint also optionally returns user information, access token and the refresh token for automatically signing user in the system if the request is performed by unauthenticated user.

Lists all the workspaces of the authorized user. A workspace can contain multiple applications like a database. Multiple users can have access to a workspace. For example each company could have their own workspace containing databases related to that company. The order of the workspaces are custom for each user. The order is configurable via the **order_workspaces** endpoint.
Creates a new workspace where only the authorized user has access to. No initial data like database applications are added, they have to be created via other endpoints.
Creates an initial workspace. This is typically called after the user signs up and skips the onboarding in the frontend. It contains some example data.

Responds with the workspace and the inviter of the invitation link with the provided slug, so that someone who opens the link knows what they join. For a member whose role the link would raise, it also responds with their current role and the role of the link.

Adds the authorized user to the workspace of the invitation link with the permissions of the link. Someone who is already a member gets the permissions of the link when they are higher than their own, and otherwise keeps their current permissions.
Lists all the invitation links of the workspace related to the provided `workspace_id` parameter if the authorized user has admin rights to that workspace.

Creates a new permanent invitation link if the authorized user has admin rights to the related workspace. Anyone with the link can join the workspace with the permissions of the link until the link is deleted. Links can't be created while both new signups and signups via workspace invitations are disabled.
Deletes an invitation link if the authorized user has admin rights to the related workspace. The link can't be used anymore afterwards.

Updates the name of the invitation link or the permissions people get when joining through it if the authorized user has admin rights to the related workspace. People who already joined keep their permissions.
Responds with the serialized workspace invitation if an invitation with the provided token is found.
Lists all the workspace invitations of the workspace related to the provided `workspace_id` parameter if the authorized user has admin rights to that workspace.
Creates a new workspace invitations for an email address if the authorized user has admin rights to the related workspace. An email containing a sign up link will be send to the user.
Deletes a workspace invitation if the authorized user has admin rights to the related workspace.
Returns the requested workspace invitation if the authorized user has admin right to the related workspace
Updates the existing workspace invitation related to the provided `workspace_invitation_id` param if the authorized user has admin rights to the related workspace.

Accepts a workspace invitation with the given id if the email address of the user matches that of the invitation. The token from the invitation email must be provided unless the email address of the user is verified.
Rejects a workspace invitation with the given id if the email address of the user matches that of the invitation.

Changes the order of the provided workspace ids to the matching position that the id has in the list. If the authorized user does not belong to the workspace it will be ignored. The order will be custom for each user.
Lists all the users that are in a workspace if the authorized user has admin permissions to the related workspace. To add a user to a workspace an invitation must be sent first.
Deletes a workspace user if the authorized user has admin rights to the related workspace.
Updates the existing workspace user related to the provided `workspace_user_id` param if the authorized user has admin rights to the related workspace.
Deletes an existing workspace if the authorized user belongs to the workspace. All the applications, databases, tables etc that were in the workspace are going to be deleted also.
Updates the existing workspace related to the provided `workspace_id` parameter if the authorized user belongs to the workspace. It is not yet possible to add additional users to a workspace.
Lists exports that were created for given workspace.

Export workspace or set of applications application if the authorized user is in the application's workspace. All the related children are also going to be exported. For example in case of a database application all the underlying tables, fields, views and rows are going to be exported.Roles are not part of the export.
Import a set of applications included in a given resource if the authorized user is in the specified workspace. This endpoint requires a valid resource_id of the uploaded file.
Uploads an exported workspace or a set of applications if the authorized user is in the workspace. The uploaded file must be a valid ZIP file containing the applications' data for future import.
Delete a resource. This endpoint mark as ready for deletion the specified resource. This operation is not undoable. The user must be the owner of the resource to perform this action.

Makes the authenticated user leave the workspace related to the provided `workspace_id` if the user is in that workspace. If the user is the last admin in the workspace, they will not be able to leave it. There must always be one admin in the workspace, otherwise it will be left without control. If that is the case, they must either delete the workspace or give another member admin permissions first.
